title: Unify ingress shim and soft-shutdown handshake for queue workers
creator: Jordan Miles
description:
Problem:
Over the past 12 months weve accumulated several ad-hoc ingress shims and shutdown strategies across the Redis and Kafka worker fleets. These differences cause observable issues during rolling upgrades and scale-downs: sudden request drops, duplicate requeues, and long tail latencies as workers fight for leases or fail to surface backpressure.

Goal:
Design and implement a single, lightweight ingress shim and a coordinated soft-shutdown handshake that: 1) provides a single contract for graceful handoff and idempotent drain, 2) surfaces per-tenant backpressure signals to the router, and 3) avoids head-of-line blocking during rolling evictions. This should be deployable to both Redis-streams consumers and Kafka consumer groups without needing distinct codepaths.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Introduce an ingress-shim library (go/ts, start with Go service runtime) that normalizes message lease semantics, ack/commit primitives, and an explicit soft-shutdown handshake API (PREPARE_DRAIN -> ACCEPT_HANDOFF -> FINALIZE).
- Implement a lease soft-eviction protocol: worker announces PREPARE_DRAIN with short TTL, scheduler/router stops assigning new work to that worker, in-flight tasks are allowed to complete or be atomically handed off.
- Add a per-tenant credit/backpressure token that is exposed via router metrics (gauge + saturation events) so the routing layer can favor non-saturated shards and apply fair-share.
- Backwards compatibility adapter for existing consumers for a 2-release window. Compatibility mode will keep current retry semantics but emit compatibility metrics and a migration flag.
- Gradual rollout plan via canary: feature-flag at process-level, then route-level, then cluster-wide.

Why this is different from prior work:
- Existing tickets focused on retry budgets, consumer prefetch and specific backoff logic. This ticket targets the orchestration contract between router and worker (handshake) and unifies the shim so both Redis and Kafka adapters use the same semantic primitives for evictions and handoffs.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Language: implement core runtime shim in Go (same as serving runtime) for low-latency integration; provide a thin TypeScript shim for Node workers used by some ingestion services.
- Atomic handoff vs. best-effort: fully atomic handoff for Redis streams (XCLAIM-based) is possible but for Kafka we will implement a lease-transfer pattern that prefers in-flight completion. We accept rare duplicate processing in Kafka during aggressive drains to avoid blocking.
- Telemetry: expose new spans (drain.prepare, drain.handoff, drain.finalize), and counters for handoff-failures, handoff-latency, and router-backpressure-events. Tie these to existing SLO dashboards.
- Compatibility: to avoid two different runtime builds we will gate behavior behind a runtime flag and add healthcheck endpoints that include "drain-ready" status.

Acceptance criteria:
- In the canary cluster, a node marked PREPARE_DRAIN stops receiving new work within 10s and completes/handsoff in <= 90s for typical 95th-percentile tasks.
- Router detects and reacts to per-tenant saturation events, reducing allocation to saturated shards within 30s.
- No increase in end-to-end error rate or token costs during rollout (<= 1% regression).
- Automated e2e test harness that simulates rolling evictions for both Redis and Kafka adapters is added to CI with deterministic assertions.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement shim and adapter for Redis streams in a feature branch; unit tests and local harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4821
2) Canary deploy Redis shim to canary cluster with feature flag enabled. Observe drain metrics and handoff latencies.
3) Implement Kafka adapter and compatibility glue. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4869
4) Staged rollout across regions with monitoring runbook.

Metrics to monitor:
- drain.prepare / drain.handoff / drain.finalize latencies (p95, p99)
- router-backpressure-events/sec and per-tenant saturation ratio
- duplicate-delivery rate during drain windows
- SLO: 99th percentile tail latency for request path that depends on worker processing

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Ingress+Shim+and+Soft+Shutdown+Design
- Local test harness: internal repo: git://redwood-internal/queue-harness (branch: ingress-shim)
- Benchmark notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aT-internal-benchmarks

Notes on related tickets:
- This ticket depends on the queue consumer refactor introduced in ENG-26789 (lease/coordination) and will consume the new prefetch metrics from ENG-7421.

Estimated effort and resources:
- 1 backend engineer (Priya) full-time for 4 sprints + 1 SRE for rollout and dashboards + 0.2 FTE of SDK/Node engineer for TS shim.
activity: 2025-02-13: Kickoff with Eng and SRE. Agreed on Go-first implementation. Action: Priya to draft PR and prototype XCLAIM handoff flow.
2025-02-21: Prototype shows Redis XCLAIM handoff reduces duplicate rate in local harness from 2.4% -> 0.5% for 1k msg bursts. See gist: https://gist.github.com/priya/ingress-proto
2025-02-28: Design review (ENG architecture). Feedback: add explicit backpressure counter per-tenant and ensure router reacts to both queue length and CPU usage. Action: Jordan to update design doc.
2025-03-02: PR #4821 opened for Redis shim. CI flaky test fixed; initial canary scheduled for 2025-03-05. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4821

2025-03-04: Discovered a race in drain.finalize when consumer restart occurs rapidly; mitigated by increasing finalization TTL and adding idempotency token. Filed follow-up sub-issue ENG-90921 for test coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Canary cluster: PREPARE_DRAIN prevents new assignments within 10s
Handoff succeeds for 95% of tasks within 90s under typical load
Router reduces allocation to overloaded tenants within 30s of saturation metric
E2E tests present in CI that simulate multi-node rolling drains for Redis and Kafka
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate processing spikes for Kafka during aggressive drains. Mitigation: Limit drain concurrency and surface duplicate-rate metric with alerting.
Risk: Backwards compatibility causing two different behaviors in same cluster. Mitigation: Two-release compatibility mode and migration flag; run compatibility smoke tests in staging.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: Sample handoff spans at low rate and emit counters instead for high-volume clusters.
